title: Should You Buy Nike Stock Before Oct. 1?
author: Will Healy
description: Nike stock has plunged to a 12-year low and was removed from the S&P 100 index due to strategic missteps and rising competition. While the stock trades at a low P/E ratio of 17 with a 4.6% dividend yield, analysts forecast continued revenue declines. The article advises investors to avoid buying before the Oct. 1 earnings report until Nike demonstrates it can reinvigorate revenue growth, as dividend payouts are exceeding free cash flow.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock has declined 80% from 2021 peak, removed from S&P 100, facing revenue declines of 3% in Q1 and 2% for full fiscal 2027, lost market share to competitors, and dividend payouts exceed free cash flow, creating financial strain.
Mentioned as a competitor that captured market share from Nike during Nike's failed online-only sales strategy, indicating successful market positioning.
Mentioned as a competitor that benefited from Nike's strategic missteps and captured open shelf space and market share.

title: Nike and Lululemon Both Hit Multi-Year Lows in September. Which Stock Is Best Positioned to Make a Comeback?
author: Leo Sun
description: Nike and Lululemon have both collapsed to multi-year lows due to weak North American sales, slowing revenue growth, and increased competition. Nike faces challenges from its wholesale retailer exit strategy and reliance on markdowns, while Lululemon struggles with soft women's apparel sales and tariff pressures. Though both face near-term headwinds, Lululemon appears better positioned for a comeback due to its cheaper valuation (10x earnings vs. Nike's 21x), despite analyst expectations for continued declines in fiscal 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock has fallen 79% from 2021 highs to $36. Flat revenue growth, 10% decline in fiscal 2025, weak North American sales, loss of wholesale retail shelf space to competitors, over-reliance on markdowns reducing gross margins, and declining EPS. CEO expects fiscal 2027 to be a 'reset' year with expected 2% revenue decline and 19% EPS decline.

Stock has fallen 81% from December 2023 highs to $99. Revenue growth has decelerated from 19% to 5%, gross margins compressed from 58.3% to 56.6%, soft women's apparel sales in North America, increased markdown reliance, and tariff pressures. Analysts expect 6% revenue decline and 27% EPS decline in fiscal 2027. However, relatively cheaper valuation (10x earnings) offers better downside protection than Nike.

Mentioned as beneficiary of Nike's wholesale retailer exit, with its Hoka brand gaining market share in the running and lifestyle sneaker markets as competitors eagerly grabbed shelf space vacated by Nike.
Mentioned as competitor that expanded market share in running and lifestyle sneaker markets by capturing shelf space Nike vacated through its wholesale retailer exit.

title: 2 Top Stocks That Can Double in 5 Years
author: John Ballard
description: Netflix and On Holding are identified as two stocks with potential to double in five years. Netflix trades at reasonable valuations with only 7% penetration of a $670 billion addressable market and expects 13-14% revenue growth in 2026. On Holding, a footwear brand gaining share against Nike, maintains strong profitability with 65% gross margins and expects low-20% sales growth, trading at 16x forward earnings with 24% expected earnings growth.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Netflix is highlighted as having significant growth potential with low market penetration (less than 45% of addressable market), expected 13-14% revenue growth in 2026, 21% consensus earnings growth, and reasonable forward P/E valuation around 20x. The company demonstrates solid acquisition, retention, and pricing trends.

On Holding is presented as a strong investment opportunity with disciplined brand-building strategy, gaining market share against Nike, improving gross margins (65.4% in Q2 2026), expected low-20% sales growth, and attractive 16x forward earnings valuation with 24% annualized earnings growth expectations.

Nike is mentioned as struggling to find growth and facing inventory and discounting issues that weigh on financial performance, contrasting negatively with On Holding's market share gains and disciplined approach.

title: On Holding (ONON) Down 13.5% Since Last Earnings Report: Can It Rebound?
author: Zacks.Com
description: On Holding's stock has declined 13.5% since its Q2 2026 earnings report, underperforming the S&P 500. While the company reported earnings meeting consensus estimates with strong DTC growth (26% YoY), Asia-Pacific momentum, and improved profitability despite tariffs, revenue missed expectations at $1,076M vs. $1,114M consensus. Management raised 2026 gross margin guidance to at least 65% and maintained EBITDA margin guidance of 19.5-20%, expecting low-20% constant-currency sales growth for the year. However, analyst estimates have shifted downward by 10.1% in the past month, leading to a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite solid Q2 earnings with revenue growth of 13.5% YoY, strong DTC expansion (26% YoY), and improved profitability, the stock has underperformed significantly (-13.5% post-earnings). Analyst estimates have declined 10.1% in the past month, and the company received a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating. The stock has an F value score and C momentum score, indicating downward momentum and overvaluation concerns despite positive operational metrics.

title: On Holding's Robust APAC Performance Strengthens Its Global Footprint
author: Zacks.Com
description: On Holding AG reported strong Asia-Pacific growth with net sales jumping 43.1% to CHF 170.5M, now representing 20% of quarterly sales. The region's momentum was broad-based across Japan, South Korea, and Greater China, with strong DTC performance and full-price discipline helping expand gross margins to 65.4%. However, the company carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating, and shares have declined 24.6% over three months.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong operational performance with 43.1% APAC sales growth, robust DTC momentum (45.7% of sales), and margin expansion to 65.4% are positive. However, the stock carries a Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell) rating, has declined 24.6% in three months, trades above industry valuation multiples (2.08 vs 1.35 P/S), and recent earnings estimates have been revised downward, indicating market skepticism despite operational strength.

Solid global momentum with revenues exceeding $1 billion, international sales outperforming domestic growth (8.4% vs 3.2%), robust HOKA international DTC growth, and 13% companywide DTC growth reflecting healthy full-price demand position the company for faster growth in the second half.

Solid global momentum with 6.8% revenue growth, strong international performance (10.9% growth, 55% of sales), double-digit growth from key brands (Merrell 11.1%, Saucony 9.9%), and broad-based international expansion across Europe, China, and APAC support an upgraded fiscal 2026 outlook.
